classification.difficultyReason: Choose a parabola with two horizontal boundary lines, calculate their four intersection abscissae, and interpret the simultaneous bounds as two disjoint closed intervals.

content.prompt: By drawing an appropriate graph, solve the inequality $-5\leq x^2-6x\leq7$.

answer.worked:
Sketch the upward-opening parabola using
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-6x\\y&=(x-3)^2-9.\end{align*}$$
Its vertex is $(3,-9)$ and its $x$-intercepts are 0 and 6. Draw the horizontal lines $y=-5$ and $y=7$.

Their intersection abscissae are found from
$$\begin{align*}x^2-6x&=-5\\x^2-6x+5&=0\\(x-1)(x-5)&=0\\x&=1\text{ or }5,
\end{align*}$$
and
$$\begin{align*}x^2-6x&=7\\x^2-6x-7&=0\\(x+1)(x-7)&=0\\x&=-1\text{ or }7.
\end{align*}$$
The graph lies on or between the two horizontal lines for $-1\leq x\leq1$ or $5\leq x\leq7$.

spec.description: Complete authored solution graph of the quadratic and both horizontal bounds. Dashed vertical guides locate the four boundary abscissae. No grid is used.
